summary: Verified the Ardit art review against the current GLBs (unchanged since Oct 28) and the Oct 29 splashes. Not on par: score 6.5 (below 8) and two majors still open. M1 is confirmed. All three skin splashes reuse one frontal victory stand and differ by a figure-box mean absolute difference (MAD) of 9.7/255 (First Bell) and 18.3/255 (Chalkline). The subject shows grain: high-pass RMS 3.96 on the pane against 0.23 on the sky. Luma never goes above 192. M3 is confirmed. In the run, the top tabard segment swings forward to 54 degrees and peaks on the same frame as the thigh (61 degrees), so it moves with no lag. The pale fins show at 1:1 in the match. M2 is downgraded to minor. Its central claim is wrong: the GLB shows the pane square in front and facing the travel direction during Lancing Run and the dash, and Muster lays the spear back 38 degrees. What remains is a camera problem. The pane's top edge tips forward, so the 52-degree camera sees it foreshortened, and Muster's key pose is no larger than an ordinary cast. M4 is downgraded to minor. The texture and tri budget is the same across the roster, and the box massing is the brief's own design. What remains is soft whites and a pane that reads as a pale board. Leftovers: 4 of 5 are still open, and the splash pauldron blow-out is closed. No sensitivity problem: the helm has a flat crown and no hood, and the face under the T-visor (nose and lips) reads as alive in every skin.

findings.title: Splashes are one static model render reused for every skin, with render grain and no highlights
findings.what:
All three splashes (base, Chalkline, First Bell) are the same frontal victory stand at t 0.92. They share the camera, the framing, the backdrop plate and the light, so only the palette and the bell change between skins.

The figure is a Cycles render of the game model, composited over the painted plate:
- the subject carries visible salt-and-pepper speckle at 1:1;
- nothing in the image goes above luma 192, so the visor, the pane and the spear head never catch a highlight.
findings.gauge: A recent League champion's splash is a bespoke painted illustration, with a staged moment, dynamic posing, cinematic light and a clean finish. Every skin gets its own composition, so the skin can be named from its splash alone.
findings.fix:
Give each skin its own SPLASH staging in ardit.py: its own clip, t, yaw, pitch, lens and sun.
- Base: a low 3/4 view, with dawn light raking through the pane onto the dial floor.
- Chalkline: dusk, braced behind the planted pavise with the spear couched, under a cold rim light.
- First Bell: a close 3/4 at first light, with the bell mid-swing.

Finish:
- Render the subject at 128 or more samples at 2x and denoise.
- Run the plate's paint pass over the subject too.
- Let the visor and pane highlights reach luma 215-230 while the card p50 stays in its band.

The 192 ceiling is a shared grade (Marund and Burdam top out at 203, Rishal at 191), so the highlight change belongs in common/plates.py and render.py for every fighter.
findings.verifierNote:
Confirmed. The numbers reproduce within 0.6/255.

Owner ruling: 'skins change material and palette, not silhouette' covers skin models, not splash staging, so it does not excuse identical splashes.

The gauge claim holds: a League skin splash is always its own composition. Severity stays major because the splash is the fighter's face in the client.

The tonal ceiling is roster-wide (pipeline grade), not Ardit-specific.

findings.verifierNote:

findings.title: Run: tabard panels kick out as rigid boards that track the thigh with no lag
findings.what:
In every in-match run, the front tabard panels hinge at the waist and swing forward with the thigh as straight pale planks. Seen from the 52-degree camera on a side heading, they fan out from the legs like fins.

The top 0.30 m segment does nearly all the motion while the lower segments hang almost straight, so the panel reads as a board on a hinge, not as cloth.
findings.gauge: On a League champion with front cloth panels, the run keeps the cloth close to the legs. It overlaps the knee and trails the shin with soft, delayed secondary motion, and never stiffens into planks.
findings.fix:
Cap the thigh push at about 25 degrees (TAB_K about 0.4, TAB_CAP about 28).

Give the lower two bones a trailing curl that grows with speed, delay the chain 2 frames behind the thigh, and add one hem flick at foot contact.

Check the result in a match frame at the default 28.5 m camera.
findings.verifierNote:
Confirmed by direct GLB measurement and by the match frame at 1:1.

This is the most-seen clip, and the plank read is plain at gameplay scale, so it stays major.

findings.title: Model finish: plain box helm and pauldrons, soft low-contrast whites, pane reads as a pale board in match
findings.what:
Several of the reviewer's points do not hold.

**The budget is roster-standard.** Ardit has 20,589 tris, a 2048 base map, 512 ORM and normal maps, and one opaque body material. Marund (21,265), Burdam (20,448) and Hesmi (19,888) carry the same maps.

**The normal map is not a gauge gap.** League's in-game champion models get their detail from hand-painted diffuse, not normal maps, so a 512 normal map is not a gap against the gauge.

**The box massing is the brief's design.** Ardit is the Aubade block, and the reviewer credits his silhouette as a strength.

**Secondary detail exists.** The close views show segmented cuirass grooves, a belt and buckle, knee cops, tabard trim and bevels on the pavise frame.

What remains is real but minor:
- the helm and pauldrons are plain boxes carrying only painted cracks;
- the whites have few crisp value breaks;
- in the match, the dawnglass pane reads as a pale board with only a faint sheen.
findings.evidence:
GLB struct read (scratch glbinfo.py): ardit 20,589 tris; marund 21,265; burdam 20,448; hesmi 19,888; all with 2048 base, 512 ORM and 512 normal.

Close views: art/renders/fighters/ardit/three_ardit.png row 3.

In match: _harness/_shots/closing_ardit_far_t477_x3.png and closing_ardit_close_red_x4.png.

The brief's pane spec ('opaque pale backing at 40%', 'keeps its transparent look') is at _design/fighters/ardit.md:64.
findings.gauge: League in-game models carry crisp hand-painted value structure (edge highlights, baked occlusion, distinct material reads) that holds at gameplay zoom.
findings.fix:
Add edge-highlight and occlusion contrast in the base bake for the helm, pauldron and pavise-frame edges, and add one carved Aubade motif on each pauldron face.

Paint the pane with a top-to-bottom dawn gradient and a crisp diagonal glint band, plus an inner rim line, so it reads as glass at 28.5 m.
findings.verifierNote:
Downgraded. The measurable parts are either roster-wide or not a gauge gap, and the massing is the brief's own design.

The soft finish and the pane's glass read are polish-level and belong in the score, not in a major.
